title: CCNA 200-301
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the Cisco CCNA 200-301 exam blueprint domains and the official cert guide topics. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: An engineer must transfer a large file reliably, and acknowledges every received segment before sending more data. Which protocol provides this behavior?
items.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable; it numbers segments, acknowledges received data, and retransmits lost data. UDP is best-effort, ICMP is control messaging, and GRE is a tunnelling protocol.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which port number is the registered default for HTTPS?
items.explanation: HTTPS uses TCP 443. Port 80 is HTTP, 53 is DNS, and 8080 is a common alternate HTTP port used informally.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: A host cannot reach the Internet but can reach hosts on its local subnet. Which configuration is the most likely cause?
options: Missing DNS D-name for the host
items.explanation: Local, same-subnet traffic needs no gateway, but off-subnet traffic is sent to the default gateway. An incorrect gateway breaks Internet reachability while local communication keeps working.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which IPv4 range is reserved for private use and commonly assigned to home LANs?
items.explanation: RFC 1918 private ranges include 10/8, 172.16/12, and 192.168/16. Home routers commonly hand out 192.168.0.0/24 addresses.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Configure and verify IPv4 addressing

items.stem: Which IPv6 address range identifies a link-local address?
items.explanation: Link-local addresses begin with FE80::/10 and are used for local segment communication only. 2001:db8::/32 is documentation, FF02::/8 is multicast, and ::ffff:/96 is IPv4-mapped.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Compare IPv4 and IPv6

items.stem: A router must forward a packet between two different IP networks. At which OSI layer does the router operate?
items.explanation: Routing is a Layer 3 (network layer) function: the router reads the destination IP address and chooses a next hop. Switches handle Layer 2 forwarding, and ports/segments are Layer 4.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Role of network components

items.stem: Which protocol resolves an IPv4 address to a LAN MAC address?
items.explanation: ARP maps an IPv4 address to an Ethernet MAC address on the local segment. DNS maps names to IP, ICMPv6 carries Neighbor Discovery for IPv6, and DHCP assigns addresses.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which subnet mask is equivalent to a /24 prefix length?
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Configure and verify IPv4 addressing

items.stem: How many usable host addresses are available in a /27 subnet?
items.explanation: A /27 has 5 host bits, so 2^5 = 32 addresses; subtract the network and broadcast addresses to leave 30 usable hosts. 14 would be /28, and 62 would be /26.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Configure and verify IPv4 addressing

items.stem: Which statement correctly describes the default behavior of Ethernet with two devices connected to the same hub? They must operate:
options: full duplex because the hub isolates collisions
half duplex because only one station can transmit at a time
items.explanation: A hub is a shared half-duplex medium, so two attached stations share one collision domain and only one may transmit at a time. Switches create separate collision domains per port.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which cabling standard is correct when connecting a PC directly to a switch port?
options: Any cable, because switches autosense direction automatically
Crossover between a PC and a switch
Straight-through between a PC and a switch
Rollover between a PC and a switch
items.explanation: Devices of unlike type (PC-to-switch) use straight-through cabling. Crossover is used between like devices, and rollover connects to a console port.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: What is the default Ethernet MTU that an IP packet must not exceed on most LAN links?
items.explanation: Standard Ethernet payload (MTU) is 1500 bytes; jumbo frames allow 9000 bytes on some networks. 1280 is the IPv6 minimum MTU, and 65535 is the IP maximum packet size, not Ethernet MTU.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which network device forwards frames based only on the destination MAC address?
items.explanation: A Layer 2 switch forwards Ethernet frames using destination MAC addresses in its MAC address table. Routers and firewalls operate on IP (Layer 3), and load balancers work at Layers 4-7.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Role of network components

items.stem: When a switch receives a unicast frame whose destination MAC is not in its address table, what does it do?
options: Floods the frame out all ports except the ingress port
Sends the frame to the router
items.explanation: An unknown unicast is flooded to all ports in the VLAN except the port it arrived on, so the destination can reply and the switch then learns its MAC. The switch does not drop, route, or ARP.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: A network engineer uses a tool that times an ICMP echo request. Which two commands rely on ICMP to test path reachability?
options: show running-config and copy running-config startup-config
items.explanation: ping sends ICMP echo requests; traceroute uses ICMP (or UDP) with increasing TTL values to map the path. The other pairs are configuration, address, and file-transfer operations.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which statement about IPv6 unicast addressing is correct?
options: Link-local addresses are routable on the Internet
Multicast is used instead of broadcast
items.explanation: IPv6 has no broadcast; multicast and link-local scoping replace it. Loopback is ::1, link-local (FE80::/10) is not routed beyond the link, and IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Compare IPv4 and IPv6

items.stem: Which statement about the DHCP process order is correct?
items.explanation: DHCP uses DORA: the client broadcasts a Discover, servers respond with Offer, the client sends Request, and the chosen server sends the final Acknowledgment with the lease.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services

items.stem: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?
items.explanation: AAAA records map names to IPv6 addresses; A records map to IPv4. CNAME aliases one name to another, and MX records designate mail servers.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services

items.stem: Which cloud service model provides the least management over the underlying infrastructure?
items.explanation: SaaS delivers finished applications the customer only uses. IaaS gives the most infrastructure control, PaaS manages the platform, and DaaS is desktop virtualization.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which WAN technology feature best fits a network that must carry voice between two offices with guaranteed quality?
options: An increased MTU on the LAN switch
A private, low-latency link such as MPLS or a dedicated circuit
items.explanation: Voice requires consistent latency and low jitter, so a private low-latency WAN (MPLS or dedicated circuit) is appropriate. Best-effort Internet offers no such guarantee.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: A host is assigned the address 10.1.1.10 with the mask 255.255.255.0. Which prefix length is this host using?
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Configure and verify IPv4 addressing

items.stem: What is the primary purpose of creating VLANs on a switched network?
options: Increase the MAC address table size
Create separate broadcast domains on the same switch
items.explanation: VLANs partition one switch into separate Layer 2 broadcast domains, restricting broadcast traffic and adding segmentation. They do not replace routing, grow MAC tables, or provide gateways.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Configure and verify VLANs

items.stem: Which encapsulation standard insert a VLAN tag for traffic between switches and is the industry standard?
items.explanation: IEEE 802.1Q is the industry-standard VLAN tagging method. ISL is an obsolete Cisco-proprietary encapsulation, 802.11 is wireless, and 802.1X is port-based authentication.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Configure Interswitch connectivity

items.stem: Which switch port mode carries traffic for multiple VLANs?
items.explanation: A trunk port carries frames for many VLANs using 802.1Q tags. An access port carries a single untagged VLAN, and monitor ports copy traffic for captures.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Configure Interswitch connectivity

items.stem: In 802.1Q trunking, which VLAN normally traverses the trunk untagged?
items.explanation: Native VLAN traffic is not tagged on the trunk; VLAN 1 is the default native VLAN on most switches. All other VLANs carry 802.1Q tags.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Configure Interswitch connectivity

items.stem: In which order do Spanning Tree Protocol port states progress on a newly enabled switch port?
items.explanation: A port begins blocked, then moves through listening and learning before forwarding frames. The states exist to prevent temporary loops while the topology is being determined.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: What does Spanning Tree Protocol primarily prevent on a switched network?
items.explanation: STP prevents Layer 2 loops caused by redundant paths; loops lead to broadcast storms and MAC-table instability. Loop prevention is its core function, not security or IP features.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: How does a switch elect the root bridge in Spanning Tree Protocol?
items.explanation: The switch with the lowest root bridge ID - bridge priority combined with the base MAC address - wins the root election. IP addresses and port speed are not part of the election.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: Which statement best distinguishes Rapid PVST+ from classic STP?
options: RPVST+ converges faster through a proposal/agreement handshake
RPVST+ is proprietary to a single vendor
RPVST+ forwards BPDUs only on the root
RPVST+ has no root bridge election
items.explanation: Rapid PVST+ (Rapid Spanning Tree) uses a proposal/agreement handshake so designated ports enter forwarding immediately, converging in seconds instead of the 30-50 seconds of classic STP.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: Which standard is used to negotiate a Link Aggregation Group (EtherChannel) between two switches?
items.explanation: LACP (IEEE 802.1AX/802.3ad) forms an EtherChannel between switches. 802.1Q tags VLANs, SPAN mirrors traffic, and LLDP is neighbor discovery.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: What is the benefit of bundling multiple physical links into an EtherChannel?
options: Reduces the number of MAC addresses learned
Adds up to 8 physical links as one logical link, increasing bandwidth and resilience
items.explanation: EtherChannel treats a bundle of up to 8 physical links as a single logical link, adding throughput and redundancy while STP still protects against loops.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: Which neighbor discovery protocol is a Cisco proprietary protocol?
items.explanation: CDP (Cisco Discovery Protocol) is Cisco proprietary; LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) is vendor-neutral. SNMP is management and NDP is IPv6 neighbor discovery.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: How does a switch construct and use its MAC address table?
options: Learns the source MAC of inbound frames and forwards by destination MAC
Uses ARP table entries supplied by the router
Uses DHCP leases to build the table
items.explanation: A switch learns MACs from the source addresses of frames entering each port and then forwards frames by looking up their destination MACs. ARP, DHCP and DNS play no role in this.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: Which PoE standard supplies roughly 30 W per port to a device?
items.explanation: 802.3at (PoE+) provides up to about 30 W per port; 802.3af (PoE) provides about 15.4 W. 802.3bt supplies up to 100 W and 802.11ac is a wireless standard.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access

items.stem: In a lightweight wireless architecture, where are roaming and radio management decisions typically made?
items.explanation: In controller-based (centralized) wireless, the WLC manages APs, radio parameters and roaming. Standalone APs make those decisions locally in autonomous mode.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Wireless architectures

items.stem: What does the SSID identify on a wireless LAN?
options: The MAC address of the AP radio
The wireless network name clients connect to
items.explanation: The SSID is the friendly network name that clients use to discover and associate with a WLAN. It is separate from BSSID, channel, and encryption key settings.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Wireless architectures

items.stem: Compared with the 2.4 GHz band, what is generally true of the 5 GHz band for Wi-Fi?
options: Higher throughput potential with shorter range and more available channels
items.explanation: 5 GHz offers wider channels and less congestion (more non-overlapping channels), so throughput is higher, but higher frequency attenuates more quickly, reducing range.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Wireless architectures

items.stem: Which encryption suite is used by WPA2?
items.explanation: WPA2 uses IEEE 802.11i with AES-CCMP encryption. WEP and TKIP (WPA) are obsolete, and DES is a legacy block cipher unrelated to Wi-Fi.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals

items.stem: Which security benefit does VLAN segmentation provide?
options: It removes the need for access control lists
It limits which devices can communicate by isolating traffic into separate broadcast domains
It encrypts all traffic between hosts
items.explanation: VLANs separate groups into distinct broadcast domains, and control-plane/L3 policies can then restrict cross-VLAN traffic. They do not encrypt or replace ACLs.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Access - Configure and verify VLANs

items.stem: A client associates to an SSID using WPA2-Personal. What establishes the encryption keys?
options: An 802.1X EAP exchange with a CA
A pre-shared key (PSK) supplied to client and AP
items.explanation: WPA2-Personal derives keys from a shared passphrase (PSK) known to both the client and the AP. 802.1X/EAP with a RADIUS server is used by WPA2-Enterprise.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals

items.stem: When a router consults its routing table for a destination, which entry is selected?
options: The route with the longest prefix match
The route with the lowest metric regardless of prefix length
The first route entered by the administrator
The route with the highest administrative distance
items.explanation: Routers perform longest-prefix-match: the most specific matching prefix wins. Metric and administrative distance break ties only among otherwise equal routes.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Determine how a router makes a forwarding decision

items.stem: What does administrative distance represent in the routing decision process?
options: The number of hops in the path
The reliability rating of the routing source - lower is more trusted
The metric of the interface speed
items.explanation: AD is a trust rating of the routing source (directly connected 0, static 1, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, RIP 120). Lower AD means the source is more preferred.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: Which routing table code represents a statically configured route in Cisco IOS?
items.explanation: In Cisco IOS the route codes are C for connected, S for static, O for OSPF and D for EIGRP. The question asks specifically for static routes.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: Which route is used when no more specific route exists for a destination?
options: The route with the highest IP address
items.explanation: The default route 0.0.0.0/0 matches any destination not covered by a longer prefix. It is typically used to send traffic to an ISP or WAN gateway.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: What is the administrative distance of a directly connected route?
items.explanation: Connected routes have an AD of 0, the most trusted, because the network is literally attached to the interface. Static routes are 1 and OSPF is 110.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: Which routing protocol is link-state and computes a shortest path first (SPF) tree?
items.explanation: OSPF is a link-state protocol that runs the Dijkstra SPF algorithm over the full topology database. RIP and (internally) EIGRP derive paths differently, and BGP is path-vector.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: How does OSPF discover neighboring routers on a segment?
options: DNS lookup of the peer hostname
items.explanation: OSPF neighbors form by exchanging Hello packets (multicast 224.0.0.5 on Ethernet) that carry area, timers and router-ID. Routing tables are exchanged only after adjacency forms.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: Which area must exist in any OSPF deployment and interconnects all other areas?
items.explanation: OSPF requires a backbone, Area 0, and every other area must connect to it (directly or by virtual link). Stub areas are a special case, not the hub.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: In OSPF, what is the router ID chosen from by default?
options: The highest loopback IP, then the highest active interface IP
A random number assigned at boot
items.explanation: Cisco routers pick the highest loopback IP as the OSPF router ID, falling back to the highest active non-loopback interface IP, and changing it requires a router-ID reset.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: Which value is used as the OSPF metric (cost) and what does it favor?
options: Cost computed from interface bandwidth, favoring faster links
items.explanation: OSPF cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth, so faster links are preferred. Hop count is RIP's metric, and delay probes are not used by OSPF.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: What is the effect of a passive OSPF interface?
options: It sets the cost to zero
It changes the network to point-to-point
It stops sending OSPF hellos but still advertises the subnet
It removes the subnet from the database
items.explanation: A passive interface stops forming neighbors (no Hello packets sent or received) yet the connected subnet is still advertised. This is commonly used on user-facing LANs.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: A router has two OSPF paths to a destination with equal cost. What happens?
options: The path learned last is preferred
The path with the lowest IP is used
One path is placed in a hold-down state
items.explanation: Equal-cost paths are all installed; the router performs equal-cost multipath load balancing across them for different flows.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: What is the purpose of TTL in the IP header?
options: Preventing packets from looping forever, decremented at each hop
items.explanation: TTL is decremented at each router; when it reaches zero the packet is discarded, so a routing loop cannot circulate packets indefinitely. It is unrelated to QoS, fragmentation identities or encryption.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity

items.stem: A router receives a packet for a directly connected subnet. Which forwarding step happens first?
options: Perform longest-prefix match on the destination IP
ARP for the destination, then send to its MAC
items.explanation: Forwarding always begins with the longest-prefix-match lookup. For an attached subnet the result is a connected route; ARP follows only after the route is chosen, and IP addresses are never rewritten.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Determine how the router makes a forwarding decision

items.stem: What is a floating static route?
options: A route learned from an unauthenticated neighbor
A default route applied to VRF only
A static route with a higher AD than the primary dynamic route, used as a backup
items.explanation: A floating static route carries a deliberately higher AD than the primary route (e.g., 200 vs an OSPF 110), so it is used only when the primary route disappears.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: What is the IPv6 default route expressed as a prefix?
items.explanation: The IPv6 default route is ::/0, equivalent to IPv4's 0.0.0.0/0. fe80::/10 is link-local, ::1 is loopback, and 2001::/3 is global unicast.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: How many usable host addresses are in the subnet 10.1.1.0/28?
items.explanation: A /28 leaves 4 host bits: 2^4 = 16 addresses, minus network (.0) and broadcast (.15) leaves 14 usable. 30 would be /27 and 62 would be /26.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Configure and verify IPv4 addressing

items.stem: What is meant by VLSM in IPv4 design?
options: Assigning variable-length subnet masks so host counts match each segment
Using the same mask everywhere to simplify design
Using a Class A default mask only
items.explanation: VLSM (variable-length subnet masking) lets different segments use different prefix lengths, so address space is matched to actual host counts rather than wasted.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Configure and verify IPv4 addressing

items.stem: What does the subnet mask identify to the host routing logic?
options: The LAN MAC of the router
Which part of the IP address is the host portion vs the network portion
The physical location of the default gateway
items.explanation: The mask marks the network bits (1s) and host bits (0s) of an IP address, which is exactly what decides whether a destination is local or must go through the gateway.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Configure and verify IPv4 addressing

items.stem: Which OSPF network type is used on an Ethernet segment and elects a DR and BDR?
items.explanation: Broadcast OSPF network types exist on Ethernet segments and elect a Designated Router (DR) and Backup DR to reduce adjacencies. Point-to-point networks have at most one passive peer and no DR election.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: What does a BDR do in OSPF on a broadcast network?
options: Backs up the DR and becomes DR if the DR fails
Injects a default route into the area
items.explanation: The Backup Designated Router is appointed to take over the DR role if the DR fails, minimizing the disruption of a DR outage. It does not inject defaults or filter LSAs.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: Which command would test path reachability hop by hop and reveal a failing router?
items.explanation: traceroute lists each hop and where the path stops, revealing the failing router or the unresponsive network between hops. The other commands show configuration, not live path state.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals

items.stem: Which routing protocol is the interior gateway protocol that would NOT be used between Internet service providers?
items.explanation: BGP is the path-vector protocol used between autonomous systems, including between ISPs; OSPF, EIGRP and RIP are interior gateway protocols designed for use within one organization.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity

items.stem: What is the effect of the route selection when both a static route (AD 1) and an OSPF route (AD 110) exist for the same prefix?
options: The OSPF route is preferred because it is dynamic
The route with the faster interface wins
The static route is preferred because its AD is lower
items.explanation: Lower administrative distance wins, so the static route (AD 1) is preferred over OSPF (AD 110) for the same prefix regardless of metric.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: Which address is used as the destination for OSPF Hello packets on an Ethernet segment?
items.explanation: OSPF routers send Hellos and AllSPFRouters updates to multicast 224.0.0.5; the DR/BDR use 224.0.0.6. 224.0.0.9 is RIPv2, and global broadcast is not used by OSPF.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Configure and verify OSPFv2

items.stem: A router has learned a network via two OSPF neighbors of equal cost. What does the routing table show?
options: No entry until the SPF dwell timer expires
Both paths installed; traffic shares across them
Only the path from the lower router ID
The path from the neighbor with the highest IP
items.explanation: Equal-cost OSPF paths are both installed in the RIB and used for load-sharing across flows; the router does not arbitrarily discard one.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Connectivity - Interpret routing table components

items.stem: Which address translation technique maps many private hosts to a single public IP using unique port numbers?
items.explanation: PAT, also called NAT overload, uses unique transport ports to multiplex many private hosts behind one public address. Static NAT maps one address to another one-to-one.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services - Configure and verify NAT

items.stem: Which DHCP options can a server deliver to a client?
options: IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS servers
items.explanation: DHCP can deliver an IP lease plus options such as mask, default gateway (option 3) and DNS (option 6). It does not assign MAC tables or OSPF IDs.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services - Describe DNS and DHCP

items.stem: Which protocol should network devices use to keep their clocks synchronized for accurate logging and certificate validation?
items.explanation: NTP synchronizes device clocks, which matters for the integrity of logged event times and for certificate validity periods. RADIUS authenticates users, SCP is secure file copy, and MLS is multi-layer switching.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services

items.stem: Which management protocol collects monitoring data by polling and also accepts unsolicited event alerts?
items.explanation: SNMP managers poll agents (port 161) and agents send traps/informs (port 162). HTTP, TFTP, and SSH are not network monitoring protocols.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services - Understand SNMP and Syslog

items.stem: What does the syslog severity level 4 (warnings) indicate about an event?
options: The event is a warning that warrants attention but service still works
items.explanation: Syslog levels run 0 (emergency) through 7 (debug); level 4 is warning - conditions that may need attention without stopping service. Reboot and death are levels 5-0 type events, and informational is level 6.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services - Understand SNMP and Syslog

items.stem: Which feature classifies traffic and prioritizes latency-sensitive packets, such as voice, over best-effort data?
items.explanation: QoS classifies, marks, and queues traffic so real-time flows like voice get priority over bulk data. NAT, STP, and SNMP serve translation, loop prevention, and management.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services

items.stem: Which first-hop redundancy protocol provides a virtual default gateway IP that fails over between two routers?
items.explanation: HSRP (and VRRP/GLBP) provides a virtual gateway IP shared by redundant routers so hosts keep a stable default gateway during an outage. OSPF, STP, and PAT serve other functions.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services

items.stem: Which transport and port does TFTP use by default?
items.explanation: TFTP uses UDP port 69 and is commonly used to move IOS images without the overhead of TCP-based FTP (TCP 21). Port 53 is DNS and 23 is Telnet.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services

items.stem: Which DNS record type identifies the mail server for a domain, used during email delivery?
items.explanation: MX records point to the domain's mail exchangers. A/AAAA give address records and PTR provides reverse resolution from IP to name.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services - Describe DNS and DHCP

items.stem: Which protocol is used by a client to request an IPv4 address dynamically on boot?
items.explanation: DHCP assigns IPv4 addresses dynamically via the DORA exchange. ARP resolves MACs, DNS resolves names, and OSPF is a routing protocol.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services - Describe DNS and DHCP

items.stem: Which acronym represents the security model of Authentication, Authorization and Accounting?
items.explanation: AAA stands for authentication (who), authorization (what they may do) and accounting (tracking what was done). It is the framework for device and network access control.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Define key security concepts

items.stem: Why should network administrators use SSH to manage routers and switches instead of Telnet?
options: SSH encrypts the session; Telnet sends data in plaintext
SSH is faster over WAN links
items.explanation: SSH encrypts management traffic, so credentials and commands are not readable in transit; Telnet transmits everything in clear text on port 23.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure device access control

items.stem: Which statement about standard numbered ACLs is correct?
options: They apply only to outbound traffic
They are examined in no specific order
They filter based on the source IP address only
They match source and destination plus protocol and ports
items.explanation: A standard ACL matches only the source address; extended ACLs match source/destination, protocol, and ports. Order matters in all ACLs, and they can be inbound or outbound.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals

items.stem: In an extended ACL statement, which fields can be matched?
options: Source, destination, protocol, and port numbers
items.explanation: Extended ACLs can match protocol (TCP/UDP/ICMP), source and destination addresses, and TCP/UDP ports, giving far finer control than a standard ACL.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals

items.stem: What does the wildcard mask 0.0.0.255 match in an ACL?
options: Any host in the 0-255 host range of the specified network
items.explanation: A wildcard mask is inverted subnet logic: the 255s are ignored bits, so 0.0.0.255 matches the last octet as any value 0-255 within the stated network.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals

items.stem: Which switch port-security violation action shuts down the interface and places it in err-disabled state by default?
items.explanation: The default port-security violation mode is shutdown: the port is disabled (err-disabled) and must be re-enabled manually or by recovery settings. Restrict and protect drop traffic while keeping the port up.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure Layer 2 security features

items.stem: Which security feature binds a learned MAC address to a switch port so it is the only allowed address (unless changed)?
items.explanation: Port security with sticky learning records the first MAC seen on a port as authorized, converting dynamically learned addresses into secure entries for that port.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure Layer 2 security features

items.stem: What is the purpose of DHCP snooping?
options: Forwards DHCP between VLANs without a relay
Trusts only authorized DHCP servers and blocks rogue servers on untrusted ports
items.explanation: DHCP snooping builds a topology of trusted ports facing the real DHCP server and drops DHCP offers arriving from untrusted ports, mitigating rogue-server attacks.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure Layer 2 security features

items.stem: Which command line is most secure for enabling remote management over the network with a hashed password?
options: enable secret, backed by SSH on encrypted VTY lines
enable password, with Telnet VTY lines
no password, authentication using a shared banner
items.explanation: enable secret stores a hashed privilege password and SSH encrypts management sessions. Plaintext enable password, no password, or merely obscured (service password-encryption) configurations are weaker.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure device access control

items.stem: Which wireless security mode is used for a corporate network authenticating users individually against RADIUS?
items.explanation: Enterprise mode uses 802.1X/EAP with a RADIUS server so each user authenticates individually. Personal uses a shared PSK and is fitted to home or small-office networks.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals

items.stem: Which ACL behavior best limits management plane access so only the admin subnet can SSH to the device?
options: A QoS mark on management traffic
A VTY access-class restricting source addresses
items.explanation: Applying a VTY access-class with an ACL that permits only the admin subnet blocks SSH/Telnet sessions from everywhere else. Port security, banners, and QoS do not restrict who can reach VTY lines.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure device access control

items.stem: What attack does configuring port security with a maximum MAC limit directly mitigate?
options: MAC flooding that overflows the address table
items.explanation: Limiting allowed MACs per port prevents an attacker from flooding thousands of source MACs to fill the switch's CAM table. Other listed attacks are not stopped by port-security MAC limits alone.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure Layer 2 security features

items.stem: Which statement about ACL processing is correct?
options: Statements are evaluated top-down until a match; an implicit deny-all ends the list if nothing matches
The most specific address is always applied first regardless of order
ACLs apply inside the routing table
ACLs refresh their rules every 30 seconds
items.explanation: Cisco ACLs are consulted in order, first match wins, and every ACL ends with an implicit deny, which is why an explicit permit must cover wanted traffic. There is no specificity reordering or timer refresh.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals

items.stem: What is the recommended minimum for protecting privileged EXEC access to a Cisco device?
options: Relying only on a login banner
A hashed password with enable secret and restricted access methods
Using the default 'cisco' password since it is familiar
Saving the password in the startup config in clear text
items.explanation: Privileged mode should be guarded by a hashed enable secret and locked-down access (SSH, ACLs). Default credentials, plaintext storage, and banners offer no real protection.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure device access control

items.stem: Which control helps prevent VLAN hopping attacks?
options: Set the native VLAN to a used production VLAN
Disable trunk negotiation and set unused ports to a dedicated unused VLAN as access ports
items.explanation: Preventing VLAN hopping means turning off DTP negotiation on access ports and parking unused ports in a dedicated VLAN; keeping native VLAN separate also limits double-tagging exposure. CDP and port security do not address trunk hopping.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Security Fundamentals - Configure Layer 2 security features

items.stem: Which statement best describes controller-based networking versus traditional networking?
options: Controllers remove the need for standards-based protocols
Traditional networking has no forwarding plane
A controller centralizes network intelligence; traditional devices decide independently from distributed protocols
items.explanation: SDN/controller-based designs centralize control logic in a controller, while traditional (distributed) networks use protocols like OSPF on each device locally. Controllers do not eliminate standards or forwarding planes.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: In SDN, which plane holds the network-wide topology and makes centralized decisions?
items.explanation: The SDN control plane is the logically centralized brain that builds the topology and programs forwarding; the data plane forwards packets as told, and the management plane covers administrative access.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: Which HTTP method does a REST client use to create a resource on the server?
items.explanation: RESTful APIs use POST to create, GET to read, PUT/PATCH to update, and DELETE to remove resources. GET and DELETE are self-explanatory, and PATCH is partial update.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability - Explain REST API impact

items.stem: Which data format is commonly used by REST APIs and represents data as key-value pairs?
items.explanation: JSON encodes name/value pairs and nested structures and is the dominant REST API representation. BPDU and VTP are switch messaging/staging mechanisms, not data formats.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: Which configuration management tool is agentless, connecting only over SSH and using playbooks written in YAML?
items.explanation: Ansible is agentless: it pushes modules over SSH and its playbooks are YAML. Puppet and Chef require agents running on managed nodes, and even Salt normally uses a minion daemon.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: What is the primary role of a YANG data model and NETCONF in device automation?
options: Standardize the structure and transport of configuration data between manager and device
Replace routing protocols in the data plane
items.explanation: YANG defines structured data models, and NETCONF carries configuration using those models over SSH, making programmatic device management consistent. They are not data-plane, wireless, or CAM features.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: What does the northbound interface of an SDN controller offer?
options: The physical cabling between leaves and spines
APIs for applications to express intent to the controller
A console port for CLI management
items.explanation: Northbound interfaces (NBI) expose application-facing APIs to state intent; southbound interfaces (SBI) program the network devices. The CLI is a management-plane console, not the NBI.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: Which Cisco product is the intent-based networking controller used to manage the enterprise campus?
items.explanation: Cisco DNA Center is the campus intent-based networking controller, translating intent into device configuration. Meraki is a cloud-managed platform rather than DNA Center, and the others are TACACS/monitoring systems.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: Which statement about the data plane relative to the control plane is correct?
options: The data plane computes the routing table
The data plane negotiates BGP neighbors
The data plane forwards frames and packets using tables built by the control plane
items.explanation: The data-plane forwards traffic using forwarding tables constructed by control-plane protocols. Routing computation and neighbor establishment are control-plane activities, logging is management-plane.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Automation and Programmability

items.stem: Which QoS marking field is used to prioritise voice traffic in modern Ethernet networks?
options: DSCP in the IP header / 802.1p PCP in the frame
items.explanation: QoS marking happens at Layers 2 and 3: 802.1p PCP bits in the 802.1Q header and DSCP in the IP ToS octet. TTL, checksum and VLAN ID are not priority markers.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - IP Services

items.stem: Two links to the same Internet service connect via a router. Which device type provides Layer 3 demultiplexing and connects a LAN to a service provider so IP hosts can communicate externally?
items.explanation: A router performs Layer 3 forwarding and is the standard device connecting a LAN to an ISP. Repeaters, hubs, and bridges only regenerate or switch Layer 1/2 signals without IP routing.
items.reference: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Exam Topics - Network Fundamentals - Role of network components
